intro: Sierra Leone's capital, Freetown, was founded as a home for freed enslaved people. The country has rebuilt after a brutal civil war.

chapters.title: Lion Mountains
text: Portuguese sailor Pedro de Sintra named the mountains 'Serra Leoa', Lion Mountains, in 1462. Bunce Island became a British slave-trading fort.

chapters.title: Freetown
text: In 1787 British abolitionists founded a settlement for freed Black people from Britain, Nova Scotia and Jamaica, and later thousands of Africans freed from slave ships by the Royal Navy. Their descendants, the Krio, shaped Freetown's culture.
Britain ruled Sierra Leone until independence in 1961.

chapters.title: Civil war and recovery
text: From 1991 to 2002 a civil war, fuelled partly by 'blood diamonds', killed about 50,000 people, and rebels became notorious for cutting off civilians' hands. UN and British troops helped end it. An Ebola epidemic struck in 2014.

keyTerms.meaning: Descendants of freed settlers, and the common language.
Diamonds mined to pay for war.
